ROOT: physical renewal, damage clearance and load-safe autonomous recovery
13 November2026Brisbane/12NovemberUTC. Original bounded constructions and source contracts, not a qualified machine or chemical material.

1. Structural recovery as an actual state transition

The owned standard-library executable ROOT_RENEWAL_CLEARANCE_AND_LOAD_SAFE_RECOVERY_20261113.py constructs equilibrium matrices and solves each state of a finite repair cycle. In an introduced1m square planar pin-jointed truss, the two left nodes are fixed. The lower-right node carries100N downward. Horizontal members connect each left node to its corresponding right node, one vertical member connects the right nodes and a diagonal connects bottom-left to top-right. Axial rigidityEA=1MN is introduced.

Healthy displacement has largest component.482843mm. Removing the diagonal leaves a connected graph with a singular stiffness matrix: the connection graph does not supply mechanical stability. Installing the opposite diagonal first yields a stable redundant state with largest component.213533mm. Removing the primary diagonal under this bypass gives.382843mm. Replacement and subsequent removal of the reusable bypass return the original state. Peak axial force among these idealized states is141.421N; equilibrium residuals are below6e-14N. These are static solver results with externally supplied ideal joints, not robot trajectories, preload transfer or physical manufacture.

The useful constructive hypothesis is to make the bypass and its load-transfer witnesses accessible to the construction machinery itself. A robot needs to install and confirm the bypass before loosening a suspect connection; control release forces while load transfers; remove the failed piece; place, lock and test the replacement; then recover the bypass and continue. Each step consumes time, motion, sensing, strength, access and finite stock. Repair of a robot that carries the only accessible tool is a separate operation, not a free helper.

An introduced one-port ambiguity is exact: a healthy spring and an unintended jammed fixture can each have1MN/m input stiffness. A50N probe produces50um displacement in either case. A motor-current, displacement or force observation at that port alone cannot distinguish the intended and unintended path. 1. Why an external wrench and compliance need not certify internal members

ROOT executed ROOT_FULL_WRENCH_PRELOAD_AND_LOCAL_WITNESS_SCREEN_20261113.py. An introduced rigid plate connects through three identical isotropic point springs k=1MN/m on an equilateral ring r=.1m. Its linear rigid-body stiffness is diagonal:
(3e6,3e6,3e6,15000,15000,30000),
with translationalN/m and rotationalNm/rad units.

UnderFz=1000N,Mx=250Nm, its relative translation is.333333mm and rotation.0166667rad=.95493degree. Net point reactions alongz are333.333,1776.709,-1110.042N. Thus the imposed resultant-force envelope does not itself bound each local member force.

Split EACH point spring into two half-stiffness branches. With no hidden preload their individual force magnitudes are166.667,888.355,555.021N, each appearing twice. Now add equal-and-opposite700N axial preload within each pair. The complete net reaction at each point, external six-component wrench and complete linear stiffness stay unchanged, while branch magnitudes become:
866.667,533.333,1588.355,188.355,144.979,1255.021N.
For an introduced1000N individual-member limit, the unpreloaded system passes, each preloaded pair passes at zero external load, but the loaded preloaded system has two overloaded members. Identical exterior measurements do not imply identical internal capacity.

This has a concrete one-dimensional realization contract. For concentric/coaxial branches with matching force-law slopek and rest lengthsL0+P/k andL0-P/k:
k(L-L0-P/k)+k(L-L0+P/k)=2k(L-L0).
Their total force law is independent ofP for everyL in the assumed elastic range. Tensile/compressive branches, matching laws, attachment, compression stability and finite installation strains must actually be constructed. The equation does not supply those properties. If paired branch forces act at the same effective point their preload cancels locally, including its resultant moment. Finite spacing or a deliberately measured internal strain may expose it.

The script also contains a weaker frozen-geometry radial-preload illustration. That example explicitly neglects geometric stiffness; a real spatially separated preload can change tangent response and become observable. It must NOT be used as a general physical proof that all external stiffness probes fail. The opposed-pair cancellation is the more useful ambiguity construction. Both are ordinary rest
